transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what's brought you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t stop worrying about everything. At work, I keep thinking our lab’s new partnership is going to mean my position gets cut, or that there’s something wrong with my data. Then it shifts to bills piling up, whether my family thinks I’m falling behind, and whether I’ve already messed up my chances of getting into grad school. It just keeps jumping from one thing to the next.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worrying that jumps from one topic to another?
About seven months now. It really started when the lab’s funding shifted and the commercial partnership changed how everything was being run.
Over these past seven months, have you also noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling sad all the time or anything like that.
Do you find it hard to stop or control these worries once they start, even when you try to set them aside?

Yeah, it’s really hard to stop. I’ll try to focus on one thing, like finishing a report or checking an assay, but then one worry leads into another. Before I know it, I’m just staring at the screen, going through every possible way things could go wrong.
Besides the worrying itself, have you noticed physical symptoms like muscle tension, feeling restless or on edge, trouble sleeping, or feeling easily fatigued during this time?

Yeah. At work especially, I feel really wound up, like I can’t settle into my chair. I’m tapping my foot, checking my messages, walking back to the instrument room for no real reason. Even normal lab noises make me jump sometimes.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling like your sleep isn't restful, during these past several months?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid close attention to my sleep.
Have you noticed trouble concentrating or your mind going blank because of the worrying?

Yeah. I missed an internal lab deadline because I couldn’t get my writing and data review organized. Lately even routine things—preparing reports, going to art nights, cooking for my family—feel like too much to keep up with.
